name: MouseWheel for VBA
shortDescription: Enable mouse-wheel scrolling for ListBox, ComboBox, Frame and UserForm in VBA — one file, two lines.
description:
MouseWheel for VBA is a single, self-contained VBA module that enables mouse-wheel scrolling for ListBox, ComboBox, Frame controls and the UserForm itself — which VBA does not support out of the box. Import one .bas file and add two lines of code.

Refactored to a high quality bar: no hardcoding, no dead code, no duplication, maximum reuse, and no MSForms library dependency (control type is detected by duck typing), so it runs on Excel/Access/Word/PowerPoint/VB6. Ships with a 21/21 passing self-test. Supports both 64-bit (VBA7) and 32-bit (VBA6) Office. Hook state self-heals if an install fails, optional diagnostics (EnableDebug), honest platform-capability reporting (IsWheelSupported/PlatformName), plus a 1-minute demo and a ready-made MouseWheel-Demo.xlsm file to verify before adopting.

Chẩn đoán tùy chọn qua EnableDebug / MWLog
Báo cáo khả năng nền tảng: IsWheelSupported / PlatformName

name: .NET SDK Portable Updater
shortDescription: Install the .NET SDK on a machine you have no administrator rights on. Sets DOTNET_ROOT and PATH, prunes old SDKs, verifies SHA-512.
description:
Install the .NET SDK on any machine — including one where you have no administrator rights.

Locked down by corporate policy, not allowed to change the machine PATH, or a borrowed lab computer: this tool covers all three.

What it does
Reads Microsoft's release index directly, picks the right SDK for the channel you asked for, downloads the archive that matches your CPU, verifies its SHA-512 against the hash Microsoft publishes, unpacks it, then sets DOTNET_ROOT and prepends the folder to your own user PATH.

How it differs from Microsoft's dotnet-install.ps1
The official script does install the SDK at user scope, but you still have to set DOTNET_ROOT and edit PATH yourself, and superseded SDK folders are left behind forever. This does all three, and refuses to install a channel that is out of support.

Privileges
User scope only. It never touches machine-level environment variables and never asks for elevation.

Kiểm tra chữ ký Authenticode của dotnet.exe sau khi cài xong.
Tự nhận diện kiến trúc: x64, x86, ARM64.
Chọn kênh LTS, STS, hoặc một major.minor cụ thể.
Từ chối bản preview và kênh đã hết hỗ trợ.
Tự dọn thư mục SDK cũ, luôn giữ lại bản mới hơn.

Một file .exe 59 KB, không cài, không gỡ.
Lưu ý: file chưa ký số. Windows SmartScreen sẽ báo khi mở lần đầu — chọn Thêm thông tin rồi Chạy dù sao.

requirements: Windows 10/11, Microsoft Excel đã cài. Không cần quyền Administrator. Phải thoát hoàn toàn Excel trước khi chạy.
shortDescriptionEn: Excel blocking macros in .xlsm files? Adds the folders you pick to Trusted Locations, with a dry-run preview, undo and an audit log. Never deletes files, never touches settings an IT admin set, no administrator rights needed.
descriptionEn:
Run this file to make your Excel workspace stop blocking macros.

Excel blocks macros and files arriving from internal shares and mapped drives by default. Editing the settings by hand means nobody remembers what was changed, and the guides you find online switch off Protected View entirely. This script only adds the folders you pick to the trusted-locations list — exactly where trust is needed, without widening the attack surface.

WHEN YOU NEED IT

- Opening a .xlsm or .xlsb at work reports that macros are disabled
- Files on a mapped drive (Z:, or a network path) open blocked
- You do not want to edit Excel Options by hand or drop Protected View

WHAT THIS TOOL DOES

1. Adds the folder you choose to Excel Trusted Locations
2. Enables Trusted Locations for the Excel version installed
3. Cleans entries carrying this tool's own fingerprints, including the ones older releases left behind
4. Records every action to a log for later review

WHAT THIS TOOL DOES NOT DO

- Does not create macros
- Does not disable Protected View, unless the ini says disable-network
- Does not trust Downloads or Temp automatically
- Does not delete files or folders permanently
- Never removes entries an IT administrator configured

SAFETY MAP: FOUR GATES

Gate 1, system directories are blocked. C:\Windows, C:\Program Files, C:\Program Files (x86) and everything underneath them. Choosing any of those is refused outright, even with /yes.

Gate 2, Downloads is never trusted automatically. Downloads is where malware is most often delivered. Trusting it means every .xlsm dropped there runs macros immediately, including files sent by strangers. A silent run refuses completely; an interactive run shows a red warning and requires you to type y before it continues.

Gate 3, network drives are asked for one at a time, default no. Every mapped drive found is asked about separately, and the default answer is no. Only autoTrustMapped=1 in the ini skips the question, and that choice is yours to own.

Gate 4, Excel running means the run is refused. Excel writes its Security settings back when it exits, so an entry added while it runs gets overwritten. A real run is refused when EXCEL.EXE is detected, even with /yes.

OPERATION: THREE MODES

Auto reads the folder list from the folders section of the ini, then asks about each mapped network drive. No paths or server addresses are hardcoded in the script.

Drive trusts an entire drive. This is the broadest action possible, so it always requires confirmation: a silent run without /yes is refused.

Folder trusts one specific folder, and handles paths that contain spaces.

PREVIEW IT BEFORE YOU COMMIT

Type the command trusted_locations_excel_safe.bat /auto /dryrun

The /dryrun mode prints what would change and writes nothing: no registry keys, no log entry, no snapshot. Drop /dryrun once you are happy. This is the mode to use when evaluating the tool before an enterprise rollout.

UNDO: THREE SECONDS, NOTHING LOST

Every real run snapshots the registry before writing anything. To roll back, double-click undo_trusted_locations.bat or run the command trusted_locations_excel_safe.bat /undo.

Only the keys that were snapshotted are restored. No folders are deleted, no files are touched and no entries are created or removed — it is a clean restore of the previous state.

LEFTOVER FOLDERS GO TO THE RECYCLE BIN, NEVER DELETED

With cleanupJunk=1 in the ini, folders named in the junk section are sent to the Windows Recycle Bin, so they can be restored the normal way. If the move cannot be completed, the folder is left untouched and the failure is reported.

The previous release used rmdir /s /q, which destroyed data irrecoverably. That is why cleanupJunk is off by default and reads folder names from the ini.

LOGGING: EVERY ACTION LEAVES A TRACE

Each run appends a line with the date, time, user and machine name: which folder was trusted, what was refused and when the undo ran. Enough for IT to reconcile the change when it matters.

WHAT CHANGED SINCE THE PREVIOUS RELEASE

1. An entry is removed only when it carries a fingerprint this tool leaves: the SV_ prefix, or a Trust_ name with a Description this tool wrote. Entries an IT admin configured survive, including the earlier entries this same tool created.
2. Leftover folders go to the Recycle Bin; rmdir /s /q is gone.
3. A Downloads gate and an Excel-running gate were added.
4. /dryrun exists for evaluation before rollout.
5. Network drives need individual approval instead of bulk trust.
6. Excel 16.0, 15.0, 14.0 and 12.0 are detected automatically.
7. A dedicated undo file is included, no command to memorise.

UPGRADING FROM AN OLDER RELEASE

Older releases named their entries Trust_, current ones use SV_. After an upgrade both can be present at once. Nothing breaks, Excel merges them, but the duplicate looks untidy.

Run the tool once and it cleans up after itself: only entries carrying its own fingerprints are removed, while anything an IT admin set stays put. Every run prints how many entries it removed and how many it left, so you can see the difference before and after.

THINGS YOU SHOULD KNOW

- A trusted folder runs the macros of every .xlsm placed in it, including files sent by someone you do not know. That is how Trusted Locations works.
- Do not trust Downloads, and do not trust a company-wide file share unless you have to.
- Do not trust a whole drive, Drive mode, on a shared machine.
- The tool writes only to HKCU; standard user rights are enough, no admin needed.
- The package contains no credentials, tokens or login details.

SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS

- Windows 10 or 11
- Microsoft Excel installed, version detected automatically
- No administrator rights required
- Excel must be closed completely before running
